newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition partners meets amid crisis.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition partners meets amid crisis.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan went into a meeting with his coalition partner Tansu Ciller on Thursday amid a deepening government crisis, Anatolian news agency said.
It said the pair began talks at Erbakan's official residence at 1045 a.m. (0745 GMT). The state-run agency did not say what the subject of the meeting was.
Deputy Prime Minister Ciller's True Path Party on Wednesday night threatened to pull out of the coalition if Erbakan did not swop jobs with Ciller by June 18.
Ciller and Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, announced on June 1 that they would seek early elections to overcome a dispute between the government and the secularist army.
Under the plan, Erbakan would hand over power to Ciller who would head a caretaker government to prepare for elections.

However, Turkish law requires the president and later parliament to approve any alteration in government, and it remains uncertain the coalition, now lacking a clear majority, could see through any such change.

The army and Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party have been engaged in a political firefight since February when a military-dominated security council ordered a crackdown on religious activity in public life.
